claims.text: Exceeding a critical fraction of HCP-prone elements causes a single-phase BCC high-entropy alloy to transition from ductile to brittle behavior.
The fraction of HCP-forming elements influences screw-dislocation core structure in BCC refractory high-entropy alloys.
Increasing the fraction of HCP-forming elements changes electronic bonding characteristics.
Ductile plastic deformation is mediated by mobile, extended screw dislocations.
Compact dislocation cores are associated with poorer low-temperature plasticity.
Compact dislocation cores produce a cleavage-prone deformation mode.
The initial material is a single-phase, compositionally complex BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The HCP-element fraction can be varied while retaining the overall single-phase structure.
Cryogenic testing accentuates composition-dependent differences in dislocation-mediated plasticity.
The fraction of occupied bonding states and bimodality of the d-orbital density of states correlate with dislocation-core structure and intrinsic ductility.
HCP elements lower dislocation-core energy and increase lattice distortion relative to an all-BCC-element refractory alloy.
The lower core energy and increased lattice distortion caused by added HCP elements drive extended screw-dislocation cores to become compact.
Compact, less-mobile dislocation configurations reduce plastic deformation capacity and cause premature brittle failure.
The proposed brittle-failure mechanism is distinct from conventional grain-boundary segregation.
Higher HCP-element fractions produce lower ductility and a more brittle fracture mode than lower HCP-element fractions.
A lower-HCP refractory alloy has approximately equal populations of edge and screw dislocations.
A lower-HCP refractory alloy sustains a more ductile response than a higher-HCP alloy under cryogenic loading.
The proposed brittle transition preferentially occurs under low-temperature, high-strain-rate loading.
At elevated temperatures or lower strain rates, creep or thermal softening may dominate deformation.
The critical HCP-element fraction for the proposed transition is undetermined.
